[ssbuffer](feat) outline start end sync and reuse (#3000)

* [ssbuffer](feat) outline start end sync and reuse

* [ssbuffer](fix) preserve shared outer-buffer sync lifecycles

Validate an enclosing lifecycle owned by a sibling transfer group before
rotating a shared flag. Report SSBUFFER rc=1 when coverage cannot be proven,
while preserving explicitly requested single-buffer mode. Never insert a
drain at an in-loop receiver wait, and match extra sync by its original flag.

Keep synchronization and buffer selection in their existing if/else form.
Cover shared V-to-C and C-to-V flags, missing lifecycles, and non-enclosing
seeds. Use valid F32-to-F16 fixpipe conversion and current to_tensor syntax
in the regression test.

Signed-off-by: 1801ZDL <1241272204@qq.com>

* [ssbuffer](fix) fix analyzeDepLoopInfo & looprange

---------

Signed-off-by: 1801ZDL <1241272204@qq.com>
Co-authored-by: wodelt <1241272204@qq.com>

++                           const std::string &activityKernelName,
++                           uint64_t &outMaxCorrId) {

++  if (corrId > outMaxCorrId)
++    outMaxCorrId = corrId;

++  if (!corrIdToExternId.contain(corrId))
++    return;

++  auto [parentId, numInstances] = corrIdToExternId.at(corrId);
++  const auto isApiOp = apiExternIds.contain(parentId);
++  const std::string apiKernelName =
++      activityKernelName.empty() ? "kernel" : activityKernelName;
++
++  for (auto *data : dataSet) {
++    auto metric = convertActivityToMetric(kernel);
++    if (!metric)

++    auto scopeId = parentId;
++    if (isApiOp)

++  apiExternIds.erase(parentId);
++  --numInstances;

++void MsptiProfiler::MsptiProfilerPimpl::completeBuffer(uint8_t *buffer,
++                                                       size_t /*size*/,
++                                                       size_t validSize) {
++  MsptiProfiler &profiler = threadState.profiler;
++  auto &dataSet = profiler.dataSet;
++  if (validSize == 0 || buffer == nullptr) {
++    std::free(buffer);
++    return;
++  }

++  uint64_t maxCorrId = 0;
++  msptiActivity *record = nullptr;
++  std::vector<msptiActivityKernel> kernelRecords;
++  std::vector<std::string> kernelNames;
++  do {
++    auto status =
++        mspti::activityGetNextRecord<false>(buffer, validSize, &record);
++    if (status == MSPTI_SUCCESS) {
++      if (record->kind == MSPTI_ACTIVITY_KIND_KERNEL) {
++        auto *kernel = reinterpret_cast<const msptiActivityKernel *>(record);
++        kernelRecords.push_back(*kernel);
++        // The name pointer is only stable while MSPTI owns the current record.
++        kernelNames.emplace_back(kernel->name == nullptr ? "" : kernel->name);
++      } else if (record->kind == MSPTI_ACTIVITY_KIND_EXTERNAL_CORRELATION) {

[CI](feat) add manual wheel upload and npuir payload OBS publish (#2868)

* Add a manual upload workflow for wheel packages

Adds upload-wheels.yml: a workflow_dispatch task that takes a list of
prebuilt wheel URLs (space/newline separated), downloads and validates
them, uploads each to the OBS nightly pypi directory with obsutil, and
regenerates index.html. Tested on the fork (URL splitting and per-file
obsutil cp fixes included).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Publish npuir payload to OBS as tarball on dispatch

Adds a publish-npuir-run job to npuir-build.yml, gated on
workflow_dispatch so the nightly schedule keeps producing GitHub
artifacts only and can never overwrite official releases:

- No input: build as usual, then publish the fresh payload.
- npuir_run_id given: skip the build and publish that earlier
  successful run's artifacts instead.

The payload (bin/, lib/, npuir-sha.txt) is packed into a plain tar.gz
and uploaded with obsutil to obs://triton-ascend-artifacts/cann/, named
ascendnpu-ir_<ver>_linux-<arch>[-<tag>].tar.gz after the official .run
releases' filename scheme. An existing object is never replaced unless
overwrite_existing is set.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Pin EPEL to the Huawei Cloud mirror in the npuir toolchain step

The runners' egress proxy serves stale EPEL metalink metadata and the
overseas mirrors 404 on the hashed repodata files, so 'yum install
ccache' intermittently fails (seen on the aarch64 build). Add a
dedicated epel-hwcloud repo pointing at mirrors.huaweicloud.com,
disable the metalink-based epel repo for the install, retry up to
three times, and verify the packages with rpm -q afterwards.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Add npuir tarball upload from prebuilt wheels

Add an opt-in Upload-Npuir job to the wheel upload workflow: it
downloads the same wheel_urls, extracts the AscendNPU-IR (bishengir)
payload bundled in each triton_ascend wheel, and publishes one
ascendnpu-ir_<version>_linux-<arch>[-<tag>].tar.gz tarball per
architecture to obs://triton-ascend-artifacts/cann/. The naming,
archive layout and overwrite guard follow npuir-build.yml's
publish-npuir-run job.

Controlled by four new dispatch inputs: upload_npuir (default false),
npuir_version (default 2.0.0), npuir_tag (default empty) and
npuir_overwrite (default false).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Support tar.gz Bisheng packages in integration tests

The Bisheng compiler install step now accepts two package formats,
selected by the file extension of the entry pinned in
cmake/bisheng-version.txt: the official .run self-extracting
installer, and plain .tar.gz payload tarballs with bin/, lib/ and
manifest.xml at the archive root, as published by npuir-build.yml and
upload-wheels.yml into the cann/ directory. Fail early with a clear
message when bishengir-compile is missing after install.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Add wheel version rewrite and latest/ refresh to the upload workflow

Sync upload-wheels.yml with the full version running on the fork:

- new_version input (default "auto"): rewrite wheel versions before
  uploading. "auto" keeps the build date but drops the time
  (3.6.0+dev20261027220530 -> 3.6.0+dev20261027); an explicit version
  applies to every wheel; "" uploads the wheels unmodified. The repack
  carries each entry's timestamp, unix mode bits and compression method
  over from the source wheel, so executables (triton-opt, *.so) keep
  +x through the rewrite, and regenerates RECORD accordingly.
- update_latest input: mirror this upload's wheels into the latest/
  subfolder, prune stale objects there and regenerate its index.html.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Remove the update_latest input and latest/ mirror

The latest/ subfolder mirror is no longer needed; drop the
update_latest dispatch input, the UPDATE_LATEST env wiring and the
upload/prune/index-regeneration block from the upload step. The main
directory upload and its index.html regeneration are unchanged.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>
